channel.title: Haas Prep
channel.description:
Plain-English prep for upcoming Berkeley Haas FTMBA lectures. Each episode walks through the assigned material for one class session so you arrive ready to think instead of translate.
Every episode names its sources in the description and in the opening. Episodes are original explanation written by a student, not recordings or readings of any course material. Nothing here reproduces slides, cases, or textbook text.
This is an independent student study project. It is not affiliated with, produced by, or endorsed by the Berkeley Haas School of Business or the University of California.

item.title: Thu Sep 10 · MBA 202 Class 6: The Cash Flow Statement
item.description:
Meets 2:00pm, N470 Chou Hall.
Profit is an opinion and cash is a fact. Why the most quoted number in corporate finance has no agreed definition, why spare cash is a warning as well as a comfort, and the enormous transactions this statement never records.
Sources used to write this episode: - Topic 04 Cash Flow Statement course notes (Even-Tov, 10 pp, Canvas): the reading assigned for this class - Libby 11th ed. chapter 12, Statement of Cash Flows (bookshelf; course cites 10th ed, so chapters not pages) - Course announcement 'Week 3 - Assignments' (Even-Tov, Sep 4), which fixes Thu Sep 10 as the cash flow session - 05 - The Income Statement - Part B_with solution.pdf (the Tue Sep 8 class deck) for continuity - bCourses assignment records - 202 vault index note
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.

item.description:

item.title: Wed Sep 9 · MBA 200S Class 5: Confidence Intervals and Hypothesis Testing
item.description:
Meets Axe 9:00am / Oski 2:00pm, N570 Chou Hall.
You never see the population, so the width of the interval is the finding, not the number in the middle. What '95% confident' actually means, why the null hypothesis is the presumption of innocence, and why a statistically significant result can be commercially worthless.
Sources used to write this episode: - Stine & Foster 3e ch 15, Confidence Intervals (bookshelf) - Stine & Foster 3e ch 16, Statistical Tests (bookshelf) - Class 5 and Class 6 Canvas pages - Course announcements (Backus, Chandra) - bCourses assignment record for Deliverable 2 - Apple - 200S vault index note
Note: Class 5 slides and both check-as-you-go exercises are locked until the morning of class
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.

item.title: Wed Sep 9 · MBA 201A Lecture 5: Introduction to Monopoly
item.description:
Meets Oski 9:00am / Axe 2:00pm, N370 Chou Hall.
The golden rule you learned in week one was the special case. Why the bakery bakes four batches and not six, why a full theater can earn nothing, why doubling the rent does not move the price, and how Costco's membership fee explains the person checking your card at the door.

item.title: Tue Sep 8 · MBA 205 Class 5: People Management and Performance Appraisals
item.description:
Meets 9:00am, N300 Chou Hall.
HR professionals guess that this year's performance score predicts 80 percent of next year's. The real answer is 27. What that does to rank-and-yank, why the best predictor of your score is how much you resemble your rater, and Reed Hastings arguing the fix is candor rather than a better form.
Sources used to write this episode: - An Imperfect Test, Cappelli, Knowledge at Wharton 2016 (study.net pack) - Say What You Really Think (With Positive Intent), Hastings, No Rules Rules (study.net pack) - MBA 205 Class 5 Canvas page
Note: Class 5 slide deck is Google Slides on the Berkeley account, not available
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.

item.title: Thu Sep 3 · MBA 205 Class 4: Motivation and Incentives
item.description:
Meets 9:00am, N300 Chou Hall.
Why don't happy cows give more milk? Satisfaction and performance barely relate. Expectancy theory as a product where one broken link kills the whole thing, why big cash rewards make people worse at thinking work, Goodhart's Law eating your goals, and why you are optimally confident only when your beliefs match reality.
Sources used to write this episode: - Class 4 slide deck, 04 Motivation MBA205 Moore (54 slides, downloaded from Google Slides) - Perfectly Confident Leadership, Moore, California Management Review 2021 (study.net pack) - What motivates us, Dan Pink RSA Animate (YouTube transcript) - MBA 205 Class 4 Canvas page
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.

item.description:
Meets 2:00pm, N470 Chou Hall.

item.title: Wed Sep 2 · MBA 200S Class 4: Control Limits and Type One and Type Two Error
item.description:
Meets Axe 9:00am / Oski 2:00pm, N570 Chou Hall.
Draw two lines on a chart and you have to choose which mistake you would rather make. Stopping a healthy factory versus letting a broken one run, why you can only reduce one error by accepting more of the other, and why the person making the call feels one of them far more than the other.
Sources used to write this episode: - Stine & Foster 3e ch 14 sections 1 and 2 (bookshelf, assigned) - MBA 200S Class 4 Canvas page - 8/28 GSI discussion transcript
Note: Class 4 slides and check-as-you-go exercises are locked by Canvas until class
Original student study material. Not affiliated with or endorsed by Berkeley Haas.
